employee_code.description: The unique primary identifier associated with the employee across Paycom

clock_sequence.description: An optional employee identifier used for imports and reporting. This is an alphanumeric field that can be up to 15 characters.

employee_gl_code.description: The unique primary identifier associated with General Ledger reporting

badge_number.description: Badge numbers are the numbers that an employee will use when logging in to a kiosk or hardware clock. Badge numbers must be unique. Employees without badge numbers may not be able to interact with kiosks or hardware clocks. Badge numbers are not required for employees to use Web Time Clocks or Web Time Sheets.

employee_name.description: This is the employee's full name in the format of Last Name, First Name Middle Initial

legal_employee_name.description: This is the employees legal full name.

first_name.description: This is the first name of the employee.

middle_name.description: This is the optional middle name of the employee

middle_initial.description: The first letter of the employee's optional middle initial.

last_name.description: This is the last name or family name of the employee.

suffix.description: A suffix in a person's name is a word or letters added to the end of a name to provide additional information about a person's status, background, or profession. Examples of suffixes in names include Jr., Sr., III, and PhD.

nickname.description: This is another accepted name to refer to the employee by. (nickname).

preferred_first_name.description: This is the employees preferred first name, this may be different than the employees legal first name

preferred_middle_name.description: This is the employees preferred middle name, this may be different than the employees legal middle name

preferred_last_name.description: This is the employees preferred last name, this may be different than the employees legal last name

preferred_employee_suffix.description: This is the employees preferred suffix. A suffix in a person's name is a word or letters added to the end of a name to provide additional information about a person's status, background, or profession. Examples of suffixes in names include Jr., Sr., III, and PhD.

employee_status.description: Employee status description, not the raw source status code.

hire_date.description: This is the date the employee was hired in the company.

most_recent_hire_date.description: This is the most recent date the employee was hired, reflective of any rehires

rehire_date.description: This is the employees rehire date if they left the company or were terminated, and then they were hired again.

termination_date.description: This is the date the employee was terminated

old_termination_date.description: This is the date the employee was terminated before they were re-hired.

term_reason.description: This was the 3 character termination reason for why the employee was terminated

seniority_date.description: This is the date of an employees length of service (tenure) for an employee to be considered for PTO Accruals or Benefits eligibility.

leave_absence_start.description: This is the date the employee started Leave of Absence and became Inactive

leave_absence_end.description: This is the date the employee ended Leave of Absence and is no longer Inactive

full_time_to_part_time_date.description: This is the date the employee started working part time from working full time

last_worked_date.description: This is the date that the employee worked last

department_code.description: Employee home Department code. This is the code assigned to the department within company maintenance and is related to labor allocations.

department_name.description: Employee Home Department description. This is the code assigned to the department within company maintenance and is related to labor allocations.

lives_in_state.description: The Lives In state is the state the employee lives in for their assigned tax profile.

works_in_state.description: The Works In state is the state the employee works in for their assigned tax profile.

sui_state.description: The Sui state is the state of their agency for state Unemployment Insurance for their assigned tax profile.

local_tax_1.description: The Local Tax 1 is the 3 character local tax code in the employee's tax profile

date_of_birth.description: This is the date of birth for the employee

marital_status_code.description: This is the marital status code for the employee, values could be S - Single, M - Married, D - Divorced, W - Widowed, or P - Domestic Partner

marital_status_description.description: This is the marital status for the employee, values could be Single, Married, Divorced, Widowed, or Domestic Partner. This could be used for benefits and tax purposes.

gender.description: This is the gender reported by the employee
values: I do not wish to self-identify

ethnic_background.description: Display description of the employee's ethnic background. The raw ethnic-background code is not exposed as this field; an unmapped code produces an empty string.

country_code.description: The 2-digit ISO country code associated with the employee's country of residence

primary_country_code.description: Country code of the selected primary address. Distinct from country_code on the employee record; may be NULL when no eligible primary address exists.

primary_address_line_1.description: This is the physical street address the employee enters as their home street address.

primary_address_line_2.description: This is the optional second line the employee enters as their home street address.

primary_city_municipality.description: This is the city the employee enters for their home address.

primary_state_province.description: The state is the state the employee enters for their home address.

primary_zip_postal_code.description: This is the zip code the employee enters as their home address.

work_email.description: This is the email address entered by the employee for communication via email

personal_email.description: This is an email address the employee has for personal uses, it is not a work email managed by the organization

secondary_email.description: This is another email address that can be used for email correspondence with the employee

primary_phone.description: The employee's Primary phone number to be reached

primary_phone_type.description: This is the type of phone for the employee's primary phone number, e.g. Work, Cell

secondary_phone.description: This refers to an employees second phone number

secondary_phone_type.description: This is the type of phone for the employee's secondary phone number, e.g. Work, Cell

primary_emergency_contact_phone.description: This is the phone number for the employees first emergency contact in case of an emergency

secondary_emergency_contact_phone.description: This is the phone number for the employees second emergency contact in case of an emergency

tertiary_emergency_contact_phone.description: This is the phone number for the employees third emergency contact in case of an emergency

primary_supervisor_ee_code.description: This is the employee code the employee will report to as their primary supervisor.

secondary_supervisor_ee_code.description: This is the employee code the employee will report to as their secondary supervisor.

tertiary_supervisor_ee_code.description: This is the employee code the employee will report to as their tertiary supervisor

quaternary_supervisor_ee_code.description: This is the employee code the employee will report to as their quaternary supervisor

primary_supervisor_name.description: This is primary supervisor's full name the employee reports to.

secondary_supervisor_name.description: This is secondary supervisor's full name the employee reports to

tertiary_supervisor_name.description: This is tertiary supervisor's full name the employee reports to

quaternary_supervisor_name.description: This is quaternary supervisor's full name the employee reports to

primary_supervisor_email.description: The email address of the Primary Supervisor assigned to the employee's position seat

secondary_supervisor_email.description: The email address of the Secondary Supervisor assigned to the employee's position seat

tertiary_supervisor_email.description: The email address of the Tertiary Supervisor assigned to the employee's position seat

quaternary_supervisor_email.description: The email address of the Quaternary Supervisor assigned to the employee's position seat

manager_level_code.description: The Manager Level code is a hierarchical classification indicating a user's managerial authority tier for routing approval workflows, security permissions, and escalation chains.

manager_level_description.description: Displays the description of the manager level, e.g. EXEC : C-Level

position_code.description: A unique alphanumeric code that refers to Position within Position Management

position_level.description: Position Level is an employee's rank or status within a specific position, in which this field displays it as an numeric code to reference for the organization's career structure

position_title_position_info.description: This is the employee's position title from position management.

status_position_info.description: This is the position status of the position the employee is assigned in position management.

business_title_position_info.description: This is the assigned business title of the employee current position from position management.

short_title.description: Short Title provides a condensed title compared to its respective position title; for example if a position's title is Chief Information Officer, the short title would then be CIO

effective_date_position_info.description: Effective dates allow changes to Position Seats on a specific date. This enables the storing of historical, current, and future information.

job_category.description: The job category assigned to the employee's position, used to classify and group similar roles within the organization

last_position_change_date.description: This is the most recent date the employee had a position change

position_seat_number.description: Position Seat Number is an alphanumeric code that refers to a Position Seat within Position Management

effective_date_position_seat.description: This is the effective date for the employee's assigned position seat. Effective dates allow changes to Position Seats on a specific date. This enables the storing of historical, current, and future information.

status_position_seat.description: This is the position status of the position seat the employee is in.

union_code.description: The Union code is a unique identifier used to reference which union the employee is apart of, if applicable

eeo1_category.description: The EEO-1 Category classifies jobs into the standardized job categories required for the federal EEO-1 Component 1 Report (Equal Employment Opportunity).

work_location_description.description: This is the work location description of the employee's assigned position.

work_location_address.description: This is the work location street address of the employee's assigned position.

work_location_city.description: This is the work location city of the employee's assigned position.

work_location_state.description: This is the work location state of the employee's assigned position.

work_location_zip.description: This is the work location zip code of the employee's assigned position.

work_location_country.description: This is the work location country of the employee's assigned position.

dol_status_description.description: This is the Department Of Labor status for the employee, whether they are Full Time, Part Time, Temporary, or a Seasonal employee.

employment_type.description: This field indicates whether the employee is a W2 employee or a 1099 employee.

pay_basis.description: This is type of pay the employee receives, some expected values could be Salary, Hourly, Commission, or By Week.

hourly_salary.description: Recorded hourly pay rate, in USD per hour. Do not assume hours worked or annualize this rate.

annual_salary.description: Recorded annual salary for Salary employees; zero for Hourly employees is not zero earnings. Use pay_type; keep salary statistics separate from recorded hourly rates. Never assume an annualization factor. For a true median use (quantileExactLow(0.5)(annual_salary) + quantileExactHigh(0.5)(annual_salary)) / 2.

scheduled_pay_period_hours.description: The Scheduled Pay Period Hours specifies the number of hours the employee works each pay period.

salary_min.description: Salary Min signifies the minimum amount an employee should be paid within a respective range.

salary_mid.description: Salary Mid signifies the mid-point an employee should be paid within a respective range.

salary_max.description: Salary Max signifies the maximum amount an employee should be paid within a respective range.

rate_1.description: This is the base hourly Rate that the employee is paid for most earnings in the system. Usually this is used for regular hours or other earnings that are designated as rate 1 earnings.

pay_type.description: Salary uses annual_salary; Hourly uses hourly_salary (annual_salary is zero). Keep compensation statistics separate by pay type; other or unknown types remain separate.

paycode_profile_code.description: A unique 3 digit alphanumeric code provided by the user that is set when creating a Benefit Eligibility Profile.

paycode_profile_description.description: description or name of the Benefit Eligibility Profile set by the user in addition to the Profile code. The description is a short name that describes the class of employees the profile is set up for.

pay_frequency.description: Schedule indicating how often the employee receives compensation payments.

pay_class.description: A pay class is a set of rules governing how employees earn time and include all rules associated with employee punches, rounding and grace periods. Pay classes are user-specific and set up by Paycom based on the information you provide. This can be found in form 10 of the employee forms.

earning_profile.description: Earning Profile will pull the name of the Earnings Profile that is assigned to an employee. Earning Profiles allow the client specify which earnings will be available for supervisors and employees to add/edit.

schedule_group.description: The Schedule Group represents the schedule the employee is apart of and the shift that are apart of the group.

last_check_date.description: This is the date the employee was paid on last

direct_deposit.description: This is a flag on whether or not the employee uses direct deposit for their pay

rules.applies_when: User asks for active employees, including current active employees; no explicit exclusion of On Leave is needed.
rules.description: Active means status Active only. Do not include On Leave or substitute the current-workforce default.

rules.applies_when: Employee lists, headcounts, current-workforce attribute metrics (tenure, age, compensation), snapshots, and cross-module employee details, including grouping by department. Does not apply to payroll, accrual, expense, or time fact aggregates, even by employee or department; use all accessible records for those. Unqualified headcounts and current employees use this default. Explicit active employees means Active only; historical or other population scope overrides this default.
rules.description: Default to current Active and On Leave. Explicit user scope overrides this default. Apply per result and blueprint slot; disclose population briefly.

rules.applies_when: Compensation statistics, comparisons, distributions and rankings unless the user explicitly selects a pay basis.
rules.description: Separate recorded Salary annual_salary from Hourly hourly_salary in their original units and separate columns. Do not assume hours worked or annualize hourly rates. Annual salary thresholds apply only to Salary employees. Unknown pay types and missing pay remain separate, not zero.

rules.applies_when: Interpreting termination_date and most_recent_hire_date together.
rules.description: Both dates can reflect offboarding and onboarding for tax, country or position changes. Do not infer the reason or override recorded status from date ordering; do not exclude such records unless requested.

rules.applies_when: User asks for current terminated status or a terminated-status count.
rules.description: Use recorded status; do not add rehire-date exclusions unless requested.

rules.applies_when: User asks for recorded terminations during a period.
rules.description: Use termination_date; current status and rehire-date restrictions require explicit user scope.

rules.predicate: <date_column> IS NOT NULL AND toDate32(<date_column>) > toDate32('1900-01-01')
rules.applies_when: Filtering for populated employee dates on fields that use default date sentinels.
rules.description: Several nullable DateTime64 fields use 1900-01-01 00:00:00.000000 as a missing/default date rather than NULL.

ambiguities.default: For unqualified salary/pay questions use recorded annual_salary for Salary and recorded hourly_salary for Hourly, separately labelled with annual and hourly units. Do not annualize hourly pay or infer pay type from zero salary.
ambiguities.clarify_if: The question asks for an hourly rate (distinguish hourly_salary from rate_1) or a per-period amount (confirm pay_frequency and scheduled_pay_period_hours).

ambiguities.default: Use most_recent_hire_date for latest/newest hired employee rankings, including rehires; use hire_date for original-hire dates and tenure unless another basis is requested. Exclude missing/sentinel and future dates.
ambiguities.clarify_if: The requested hire-event history cannot be answered from the documented snapshot dates; explicit original/recent-hire wording selects the corresponding field without clarification.

schema_notes: Types are the existing logical ClickHouse-compatible contract, not verified MySQL source types. Trino discovery reports deployed physical column types separately.

Trino views map string columns to VARCHAR, decimal columns to DECIMAL(18,6), position_level to INTEGER, and direct_deposit to SMALLINT. Verify source ranges and direct_deposit values of 0 or 1; casts do not enforce these business constraints.

DateTime64(6) columns target TIMESTAMP(6) in Trino. Confirm source DATE, DATETIME, or TIMESTAMP types and timezone semantics before casting; a cast does not establish source precision or non-null guarantees.
The declared employee grain is intended, not verified for joined MySQL reporting views. Validate child-table uniqueness or current-row selection before COUNT(*) is used as employee count.
pay_type is LowCardinality(Nullable(String)).
labor_allocation_key_1 through labor_allocation_key_20 join independently to labor_allocation using client_code + proc_center + join_key.

Date fields with observed 1900-01-01 00:00:00.000000 sentinel values include rehire_date, termination_date, old_termination_date, seniority_date, leave_absence_start, leave_absence_end, full_time_to_part_time_date, last_worked_date, date_of_birth, and last_check_date.

notes: client_code and proc_center are enforced by the configured backend row-access mechanism and omitted from exposed columns and joins.

row_scope.enforced_by: ClickHouse row policy on the ClickHouse path; secured views or equivalent tenant and employee-access policies on the Trino path. Sending identity alone does not enforce row access.

dbpcm_warehouse.employee_change.description: NOT a current-state table — use the employee table for current values. Field-level audit trail of employee master-data changes. Each row captures one field-level update on an employee record: which field changed, the old and new descriptions, the actor who made the change, and timing.
dbpcm_warehouse.employee_change.grain_note: Physical storage key is (proc_center, client_code, id). Analytic grain is one row per field-level change event per employee. This grain is unverifiable against live data while the MCP is down.
dbpcm_warehouse.employee_change.primary_key_note: No business primary key is exposed. The physical ORDER BY key is (proc_center, client_code, id).

temporal.note: change_time_added is when the change was recorded in the system; effective_date is when the change takes effect. These are distinct — do not treat them interchangeably.

id.description: Internal storage row id (deduplication); part of the physical ORDER BY key. Use FINAL to collapse duplicate versions and retrieve the latest record per (proc_center, client_code, id).

employee_code.description: Unique employee identifier in Paycom. Canonical join key to employee table.

changed_field.description: Name of the field that was updated on the data source. Values are UNOBSERVED (dev MCP is down) and client-defined. Interpret via resolveValues(changed_field, <concept>) against the client's configured field label space. Examples of common changed fields include: "Position Seat ID", "Location", "Pay Basis", "Rate 1", "Address", "Hourly Salary", "Last Pay Change", "Salary". Do not hardcode a fixed enum of values.

change_description.description: Free-text description of the record change that occurred.

old_value_description.description: Description of the old (previous) value before the change. This field may contain sensitive data such as address or salary information.

new_value_description.description: Description of the new value after the change. This field may contain sensitive data such as address or salary information.

change_time_added.description: Timestamp when the change was recorded in the system. Row visibility is governed by row policy.

change_by_username.description: Username of the user who made the change. Row visibility is governed by row policy.

change_by_usertype.description: Type of user who made the change. Dictionary semantics: values represent roles such as employee, client admin, or regular user. Values are UNOBSERVED in the dev MCP. Interpret via resolveValues(change_by_usertype, <concept>) against the client's configured user types. Do not hardcode enum values.

effective_date.description: Date when the change goes into effect. Use for as-of analysis of when a change took effect, distinct from when it was recorded (change_time_added).

change_events.defined_over: deduplicated rows (apply dedup_first rule before aggregation)

employees_changed.defined_over: deduplicated rows (apply dedup_first rule before aggregation)

rules.applies_when: Employee-detail requests, even with a period filter. Does not apply to period fact totals or aggregates, including by employee or department; use all accessible records.
rules.description: Default to current Active and On Leave. Explicit user scope overrides this default. Apply per result and blueprint slot; disclose population briefly. Filter via a tenant-scoped employee semijoin to avoid duplicating records.

rules.applies_when: any aggregation or analysis on this table
rules.description: The ONLY canonical deduplication pattern is `FROM employee_change FINAL`. The ReplicatedReplacingMergeTree('{__version__}') requires FINAL to deliver correct state. Aggregation without FINAL is INCORRECT — it can include stale duplicate versions. Note that replica convergence after merges means non-FINAL reads may see divergent counts across replicas.

rules.applies_when: analyzing changes that took effect
rules.description: Filter to effective changes only. This is a data-team-defined flag. Use when the question concerns changes that have taken effect, not all recorded changes.

rules.applies_when: analyzing changes after a reference point (e.g., a termination date or audit cutoff)
rules.description: Use a bound parameter (never interpolate values directly) to ask for effective changes occurring after a specific date. Always prefer using named parameters — e.g., toDateTime64({reference_effective_date}, 6) — through the MCP's parameter binding.

resolves_to: Rows where changed_field identifies a salary/rate field (e.g., 'Salary', 'Rate 1', 'Hourly Salary')
Old and new value descriptions carry the before/after salary details
ambiguities.clarify_if: client's changed_field label space is unobserved; may differ across tenants

resolves_to: Rows where changed_field identifies a position/role/title field
ambiguities.clarify_if: client's changed_field label space is unobserved; may differ across tenants

resolves_to: Rows where changed_field identifies a role or title field
ambiguities.clarify_if: client's changed_field label space is unobserved; may differ across tenants

resolves_to: All rows in the table represent the full change history
For history vs what-took-effect, additionally filter is_effective = 1

schema_notes: Table and employee_change_rls row policy ship together in schema MR !9 (V4-551040).
Table uses ReplicatedReplacingMergeTree with __version only (no __deleted column in DDL). FINAL collapses versions; there are no tombstone semantics.
Descriptions derived from schema DDL + data-team dictionary without live data verification (provisional pending MCP restoration). Value spaces are UNOBSERVED.
The `sensitive` flag on old_value_description and new_value_description is metadata-only today (no consumer-side masking is enforced).
Results are additionally employee-filtered per principal via user_employee_access, beyond the tenant scope expressed in row_scope.
Table is partitioned by toYYYYMM(change_time_added).

2026-10-07 hygiene: removed the stale is_effective column entry (absent from the live ClickHouse table; never served on either backend's discovery surface) and corrected the effective_date type to Nullable(Date32) (live DDL truth).

dbpcm_warehouse.expense.description: Expense Management line-item table with snake_case column names. Contains individual employee expense entries submitted through the Expense Management module, including reimbursable expenses, corporate card purchases, mileage and trip details, and per diem payments. One row represents one individual expense line item; an expense report can contain many line items, and one payroll transaction can pay many expense line items.
dbpcm_warehouse.expense.grain_note: Natural grain is one row per expense_id within tenant scope. expense_report is not unique because one report can contain many expense line items. For paid-spend analysis, multiple line items may share employee_code and expense_paid_date, but expense_id remains the row-level grain.
dbpcm_warehouse.expense.primary_key_note: Tenant-scoped expense line-item key. expense_id must not be used across clients or processing centers by itself. The physical ORDER BY key is (proc_center, client_code, expense_id).

temporal.note: Constrain at least one expense time dimension before broad aggregation. Use expense_paid_date for paid timing; use individual_expense_date for when the expense was incurred; use date_time_submitted for submission; use approved_date for approval; use purchase_date, post_date, and import_date for corporate card transaction timing; use card_issue_date and card_expiration_date for the card validity period.

dbpcm_warehouse.payroll.description: Payroll register line-item table. Contains paycheck components such as earnings, deductions, taxes, benefits, employer taxes, and net-pay distributions. Not one row per paycheck. Earnings are the finalized stage of total_earning after the pay period closes; use earnings-register rows for finalized earnings, and total_earning for in-progress periods. Do not add both sources for the same covered earnings. A cross-source report requires a verified finalization boundary and overlap handling, not just calendar dates.
dbpcm_warehouse.payroll.grain_note: Payroll is a line-item register table. The physical deduplication grain is represented by dedup_hash, which is derived from payroll business attributes including gross_to_net_key, profile_code, type_code, type_rate, employee_code, distributed_job_allocation_key, pay_date and check_number. Multiple payroll rows may exist for the same employee and pay_date.
dbpcm_warehouse.payroll.primary_key_note: No business primary key is exposed. The physical storage grain is represented by dedup_hash together with tenant scope.

temporal.note: Constrain at least one payroll time dimension before broad aggregation. Unqualified payroll or gross earnings for a year, month, or date range use pay_date (check/payment date), including payments for work in an earlier period. Disclose the basis as "Based on pay dates in the requested period." Explicit work-performed or pay-period-coverage requests use pay_period_start_date and pay_period_end_date instead. If a boundary-crossing pay period requires a choice of inclusion or proration, clarify that choice; do not invent an allocation or silently substitute pay_date. Ingestion freshness is not a payroll date basis.

dbpcm_warehouse.punch_pair.description: Employee matched In/Out and generated time records. Salaried approved time off can create a punch; salaried timesheet punches can be populated automatically at pay-period end. Presence or absence of these records does not establish whether a salaried employee clocked in. Each row captures a paired record (day, lunch, break, or transfer punch types). Not individual unpaired punches — use the Punches table for raw single-clock events.
dbpcm_warehouse.punch_pair.grain_note: Physical storage key is (proc_center, client_code, table_source, id). Analytic grain is one row per matched In/Out punch pair for an employee. This grain is unverifiable against live data while the MCP is down.
dbpcm_warehouse.punch_pair.primary_key_note: No business primary key is exposed. The physical ORDER BY key is (proc_center, client_code, table_source, id).

temporal.note: in_punch_time and out_punch_time are the ACTUAL punch timestamps, not rounded values. punch_date is the calendar date on which the pair is recorded. Use punch_date for day-level aggregation; use in_punch_time or out_punch_time for precise clock-time analysis.

dbpcm_warehouse.time_off_request.description: Employee accrual-event log containing all types of accrual events, not only PTO or approved time-off requests. Includes time-off requests, payout requests, and other accrual activity across workflow statuses and leave categories. Available types vary by client and period; discover event_type, status, and earn_code/earn_description for the requested scope. Event-level records, not an accrual-balance table. For time-off-taken questions, assume approved time-off requests were taken; disclose this assumption. These hours are not verified payroll-paid hours or posted balance usage.
dbpcm_warehouse.time_off_request.grain_note: Event-level accrual log. No reliable exposed row id; do NOT assume uniqueness by employee_code, request_date, earn_code, or status. Granularity is ONE ROW PER DAY of a request (see request_date), so SUM(hours) over a request_date range is exact. Logical analysis grain: one accrual event/day row.
dbpcm_warehouse.time_off_request.primary_key_note: No reliable unique primary key is exposed.

employee_code.description: Employee identifier; canonical join key to employee.

request_date.description: The single day the time off / accrual event is for. Granularity is ONE ROW PER DAY — a multi-day request creates one row per day — so SUM(hours) over a request_date range is exact (no hidden multi-day spans). Use for when the leave/event occurs.

hours.description: Hours attached to the accrual event. Filter status and event_type for approved request hours; treat approved time-off requests as assumed taken, disclose the assumption, and distinguish payroll-paid hours and posted balances.

earn_code.description: Accrual earning code. CLIENT-DEFINED and drifts over time — resolve concepts to codes via resolveValues(earn_code, <concept>), do not hardcode. Interpret with earn_description and the requested period. Context active_accrual_earnings lists distinct earning codes and descriptions from active accrual assignments across the whole client, using the latest non-deleted definition effective now. It is not limited to the caller's accessible employees and does not establish historical event values or classify every code as vacation.

event_type.description: Accrual event category across all event types. Listed and observed values are not exhaustive; resolve available types in the requested client and period. Do not assume all rows are time-off requests.

dbpcm_warehouse.total_earning.description: Summarized daily earning entries per employee by earning code. Aggregates timecard outcomes into daily buckets for payroll cost analysis and labor reporting. These are the in-progress earnings that are fixed/finalized and moved to payroll after the pay period closes. Use total_earning for open-period earnings and payroll earnings-register rows for finalized periods. These are stages of the same earnings lifecycle, not independent additive amounts. Never sum or union both for the same covered earnings without a verified period-close boundary and overlap handling. Physical deletion from total_earning is not guaranteed by this contract. Not individual punch pairs — use punch_pair for matched In/Out detail.
dbpcm_warehouse.total_earning.grain_note: Physical storage key is (proc_center, client_code, table_source, id). Analytic grain is one row per employee × punch_date × earn_code × department_code bucket. This grain is unverifiable against live data while the MCP is down.
dbpcm_warehouse.total_earning.primary_key_note: No business primary key is exposed. The physical ORDER BY key is (proc_center, client_code, table_source, id).

temporal.note: Constrain at least one time dimension before broad aggregation. Use punch_date for the day of the timecard entry; use pay_period_start_date and pay_period_end_date for period-covered analysis. Also used for cross-table total_earning↔payroll joins via employee_code + overlapping pay periods.

rules.predicate: payroll.amount WHERE register_type = 'EARN'; date basis pay_date
rules.applies_when: unqualified gross earnings for a year, month or date range
rules.description: Use payroll register earnings and pay_date for this default, across all authorized fact records unless explicitly scoped. Timecard or in-progress earnings are a separate measure from total_earning, using its documented date basis. Missing recent payroll rows do not authorize substituting total_earning or prove a period is open or unpaid. Combining sources requires a verified finalization boundary and overlap handling. Explicit timecard and work-period requests override defaults.

rules.description: MCP owns storage-version deduplication. Its ClickHouse execution layer applies the final=1 query setting; agent SQL and blueprint templates do not need an explicit FINAL clause. Do not reject an MCP query merely because its SQL lacks FINAL, and do not invent __version or __deleted predicates. This storage-level deduplication does not remove overlap between payroll and timecard earnings.

DO NOT use this as a WHERE filter when querying by pay period — use pay_period_start_date and pay_period_end_date in the query predicate instead.

Row policies shipped in schema MR9 with tenant + employee-level gating via dbpcm_warehouse_security.user_employee_access.
Results are additionally employee-filtered per principal beyond the tenant scope expressed in row_scope.
